Welcome to the computational lab of **Advanced Physical Chemistry**. Over ten experiments you will use density functional theory (DFT) the way researchers do: choose a method, run real quantum-chemistry jobs on a shared server, compare your numbers with high-level reference data, and decide which results you can trust. Every experiment comes from real benchmark databases, and every one hides a lesson about where DFT works well and where it doesn't.

## How every experiment works

::: {.steps}
1. **Warm up.** A short concept check (not graded) brings back what you need.
2. **Meet the molecules.** Rotate them in 3D, check charge and spin, and download the geometries.
3. **Predict first.** Commit to what you *think* will happen before you compute anything.
4. **Run the jobs** in [Q-Chem through IQmol](guides/iqmol-setup.qmd). Each page gives you a checklist and a ready-made input for every job.
5. **Enter your results.** The page checks your arithmetic, without giving away the answer, and draws the plots.
6. **Explain.** Answer the questions using your own tables and plots, and see how your predictions held up.
7. **Submit** your file through the Microsoft Form (sign in with your Florida Tech email).
:::

Your work is saved automatically **in this browser** as you go. To switch computers, download your submission file and load it on the other machine.

The class comparison for each experiment appears on [Class results](class-results.qmd) after the deadline.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Where these experiments come from
The experiments are adapted from a tutorial review on the often-overlooked details of DFT calculations [@morgante2020]. The calculations use Q-Chem [@epifanovsky2021] through the free IQmol interface [@iqmol].
:::
